To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the sensitivity of Salmonella strains isolated from patients with Salmonella infections in 1975--1979 was studied and that S. typhi-murium strains were the most resistant.
the sensitivity of the Salmonella strains to antibiotics in 5 years of observation (1975-1978) was not changed, and that the resistance to antibiotics was higher among S. typhiumurium strains.
the sensitivity of the Salmonella strains to the antibiotics tested was not changed significantly during the period of 1975-79.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the necessity of the wide use of the antibiotics in the treatment of salmonellosis and with the necessity of using the antibiotics of different groups for the therapy in order to prevent the development of the resistant strains.

the problem of the antibiotic sensitivity of Salmonella strains isolated in 1975--1977, the period of the highest incidence of salmonellosis and the most frequent isolation of Salmonella in the USSR, in comparison with the results obtained in other countries and in our country in previous years.
the necessity of the wide use of antibiotics in the therapy of salmonellosis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

in 1975, 1976 and 1979 the Salmonella strains isolated in the country preserved their high sensitivity to most of the antibiotics used in therapy and that the resistance of S. typhymurium was the most significant and most widespread.

the Salmonella strains of all serotypes isolated in 1975, 1976, 1977 and 1978 were more sensitive to the antibiotics used in comparison with those isolated in 1979 and that the sensitivity of S. typhymurium was the most variable in the course of the years.
the sensitivity levels to the antibiotics used in therapy were not changed in the Salmonella strains of different serotypes in the last 5 years.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the sensitivity to the main antibiotics used for treatment of patients with salmonelloses was preserved in 1975--1979 and the resistance levels to them were not increased.
the Salmonella strains studied were sensitive to the antibiotics used and the resistance to the antibiotics used in the therapy was not increased in the Salmonella strains of S. typhymurium.
the resistance levels to the antibiotics studied were higher in S. typhi and S. typhosum, lower in S. paratyphi B and the highest in S. tympimurium.
The main takeaway from our work is that
in 1975--1977, the Salmonella strains were more sensitive to the antibiotics used, and in 1979 the strains were more resistant.
S. typhi and S. paratyphi B were sensitive to all the antibiotics tested.
the sensitivity of S. typhymurium to antibiotics is lower and the resistance of this pathogen is increasing.
